pr_title: [release/8.0] Update binder gen emitted-interceptor nullability to match framework impl
pr_body:
Backport of #91180 to release/8.0
Fixes #90987 for 8.0.

## Customer Impact

Updates null input handling by the generated replacement binding methods to align with the reflection-based implementation. This follows the general user expectation of consistency between the two implementations.

## Testing

Automated null handling tests have been added for all parameters of all binder methods. They assert the same behavior for source-gen and reflection. Some null refs in the reflection binder were fixed as well. This also provides complete build coverage for all binding inputs.

## Risk

Low. It's a contained fix for an off-by-default component.

cc @carlossanlop.

issue_context.title: Config generator doesn't match nullability semantics of built-in Bind
comments:
Tagging subscribers to this area: @dotnet/area-extensions-configuration See info in [area-owners.md](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/main/docs/area-owners.md) if you want to be subscribed.
Issue Details
The built-in Bind method annotates the object as nullable: ```C# public static void Bind(this IConfiguration configuration, object? instance) ``` and then explicitly nops if it's null: ```C# if (instance != null) { ... } ``` In contrast, the code generated by the generator annotates it as non-nullable and throws an exception if it's null, changing the semantics when using the source generator. ```C# if (obj is null) { throw new ArgumentNullException(nameof(obj)); } ``` (It also names the parameter `obj` instead of `instance`.)
Author: stephentoub
Assignees: -
Labels: `untriaged`, `area-Extensions-Configuration`
Milestone: -

review_comments: Nit/question (not blocking): Would `is not null` be preferred here? `is (not) null` is used through most of this code, but there are some `!= null`s mixed in.
Per https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/91359#discussion_r1312214668, we could def clean up aspects of the reflection code later.

This was missed in the interceptors change, where we switched away from using fully qualified names for the top level replacement binders (emitted in global namespace). With the Roslyn feature, we now emit all the code within a namespace (same one needed for the granular interceptors opt-in btw), and emit the `usings` within the namespace.
These comments with the table of scenarios is really helpful
Yeah the source gen impl followed this closely.
